placement.details: optima-m7-summary-worker.service. t3 enqueues/polls fixed-purpose S3 jobs and promotes completed reports.
optima-collection-watchdog; enabled EventBridge Scheduler at :05 and :35 UTC (:05 and :35 CET); reserved alert state is in S3.
semaphore, db.t4g.micro, MySQL 8.4.9, 20 GiB gp3 / 3,000 IOPS; constellation_operations and metadata_engine schemas.
data-collection-059416028963-us-east-1-an / research-data/. Logical stores in the schematic share this bucket.
Committed observation tables, metadata observations and owner-specific curated releases; verification receipts gate publication.
Historical provider reservations, leases and cross-host USPTO/EDINET pacing use RDS. EODHD uses one conditional-write S3 counter across t3 and m7; daily ceiling 98,000, rolling rate 900/minute.
t3 role lambdaEc2ForEc2Instance; m7 role constellation-backfill-worker. API credentials and scoped database credentials are separate.

evidence: Live EC2 and RDS describe calls
Live systemd unit and template-instance inventories through SSM
Live Lambda configuration and EventBridge Scheduler configuration
limitations: Placement and design, not a certificate of complete data coverage or absence of source failures.
Small API capture and daily readback remain on t3; document processing, migrated capture, publishers and summaries run on m7.

Metadata-controller cycles currently dispatch the metadata publisher unconditionally, so they can wake m7 even with empty queues; the guard protects idle shutdown but this is not purely backlog-triggered startup.
No event/model-stage systemd services found on the inspected hosts; their monitoring registry entries do not prove deployment.
Historical source modules still contain older c7i labels; the live worker instance is m7i.large.
AWS acceptance of an SNS publish does not prove notification delivery.
Worker service counts are not job throughput or simultaneous database claim counts.
